results.content:
The Sharing and Visibility Architect exam broke my study routine, in a good way.
For every cert before it, I could read the docs, run the Trailhead modules, pass. This one kept punishing that. The practice questions weren't asking "what does a sharing rule do" — they were asking which three mechanisms combine for 40,000 users and external access without melting record recalculation.
So I stopped reading and started breaking things. Spun up a dev org, built a role hierarchy, then spent evenings misconfiguring it on purpose — flipping an org-wide default to Private and watching exactly who lost access, timing how long ownership changes took to recalculate. [...] Put together, that is the whole bet. The term peaked and stalled. The actual integrations keep climbing anyway. And the demand underneath both, people wanting their own AI wired into their tools, is still building. If that holds, MCP is not late, it is early.
Mobile first never meant no app. It meant the interface changed, the job stayed the same. MCP first is the same trade, except earlier. We are building for a room that has not filled up yet.
